media:group.media:title: Mission-Ready Advanced Manufacturing
media:group.media:description:
Johns Hopkins APL researchers are advancing manufacturing to make critical parts more consistent, reliable and predictable.
By combining advanced sensing, data-driven approaches and artificial intelligence with new manufacturing techniques, APL is working to better understand how parts are made, identify variations in the process and build greater confidence into the finished product. Hear from APL experts about the challenges facing advanced manufacturing today and the technologies helping shape its future.
Learn more about APL’s work in advanced manufacturing: https://jhuapl.link/957

entry.title: Engineering America at 250: Spotlight on Mechanical Engineering

media:group.media:title: Engineering America at 250: Spotlight on Mechanical Engineering
media:group.media:description:
As part of the National Academy of Engineering's commemoration of America's 250th anniversary, the Engineering America campaign highlights the disciplines and breakthroughs that have shaped our nation and the engineers advancing what comes next.
This spotlight focuses on mechanical engineering, featuring APL's Brian Olson, chief scientist in the Air and Missile Defense Sector and a Fellow of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers, and Charles Meneveau, L.M. Sardella Professor of Mechanical Engineering at JHU's Whiting School of Engineering and a member of the National Academy of Engineering. Their conversation explores the growing role of artificial intelligence in mechanical engineering and how expertise across APL and JHU comes together to develop solutions to critical challenges.

entry.title: Using Ultrasound to Detect Early-Stage Stress Fractures

media:group.media:title: Using Ultrasound to Detect Early-Stage Stress Fractures
media:group.media:description:
Johns Hopkins APL researchers are developing Osteo Surface Echo Evaluation (OsteoSEE), a noninvasive technology that uses ultrasound-generated surface acoustic waves to identify microstructural changes and early-stage fractures in bone without ionizing radiation.
In testing, OsteoSEE has detected fractures smaller than 0.5 millimeters, with the potential to support earlier intervention for military personnel and others at risk of overuse injuries. The technology was named a 2026 R&D 100 Award winner.

entry.title: Mars-Bound APL Instrument to Provide New Look at Martian Moons

media:group.media:title: Mars-Bound APL Instrument to Provide New Look at Martian Moons
media:group.media:description: The Johns Hopkins APL-built MEGANE instrument launched aboard JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft on Oct. 19. The instrument will measure the elemental composition of Phobos, helping scientists investigate the origins of the Martian moon. https://jhuapl.link/0664cd

entry.title: From the Battlefield to Breast Cancer

media:group.media:title: From the Battlefield to Breast Cancer
media:group.media:description:
After his wife’s breast cancer diagnosis, Johns Hopkins APL engineer Dave Porter began exploring how AI-powered data fusion technology developed for military applications could help tackle a different challenge.
APL researchers are applying data fusion and image registration to help radiologists align medical images and identify potential breast lesions more quickly and accurately.
Learn more: https://jhuapl.link/cjf

media:group.media:title: Engineering America at 250: Spotlight on Materials Engineering
media:group.media:description:

entry.title: DART: The Impact That Made History

media:group.media:title: DART: The Impact That Made History
media:group.media:description:
Four years ago, NASA’s DART spacecraft, built and managed by Johns Hopkins APL, intentionally struck the asteroid Dimorphos — demonstrating for the first time a technique that could one day help defend Earth from a hazardous asteroid.
Learn more: https://jhuapl.link/DART

entry.title: Sea++ Expands APL's Maritime Testing Capabilities

media:group.media:title: Sea++ Expands APL's Maritime Testing Capabilities
media:group.media:description: APL's new research vessel expands the Laboratory's ability to test and evaluate emerging maritime technologies in realistic operational environments. Designed as a flexible, modular platform, the vessel supports autonomous systems, sensors, communications, and other mission-critical capabilities, helping researchers move innovations from the lab to the water faster.​

entry.title: Fieldable Quantum Sensors Could Revolutionize Warfighter Safety

media:group.media:title: Fieldable Quantum Sensors Could Revolutionize Warfighter Safety
media:group.media:description:
Chemical and biological threats in contested environments come in myriad, ever-evolving forms — and scientists at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland, are developing a sensing platform with the potential to keep pace. APL's sensor takes the principle behind nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, or NMR, and aims to shrink it down from a room-sized apparatus to a fieldable device that could be carried in a backpack.
Read the full article: https://www.jhuapl.edu/news/news-releases/260916-quantum-magnetometry

entry.title: How Snakes Are Inspiring a New Generation of Thermal Sensors

media:group.media:title: How Snakes Are Inspiring a New Generation of Thermal Sensors
media:group.media:description: Researchers at the Johns Hopkins APL are exploring a new approach to sensing by taking inspiration from biology. Instead of relying solely on traditional electronics, their work draws from the remarkable heat-sensing abilities found in nature to develop compact, biologically driven infrared sensing technologies. https://jhuapl.link/wwo

entry.title: Building NASA's Dragonfly: Behind the Scenes of Integration and Testing

media:group.media:title: Building NASA's Dragonfly: Behind the Scenes of Integration and Testing
media:group.media:description:
Building a rotorcraft designed to explore Saturn's moon Titan takes years of careful assembly, integration, and testing.
Go behind the scenes inside the cleanroom at Johns Hopkins APL where engineers and technicians spent months bringing together the components that will become NASA's Dragonfly spacecraft. This compilation showcases key milestones from February through June 2026 as Dragonfly moved closer to launch.
Dragonfly is NASA's mission to explore Titan, the largest moon of Saturn, searching for the chemistry that may help answer questions about the origins of life.
Watch Eye on Dragonfly Live: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_SONK-B3G6Q
Learn more: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/dragonfly/
